cell.condition_text: Applies to legislative agents' reporting of expenditures for meals and other food and beverages; itemization required only once cumulative calendar-year food/beverage payments to/for a particular covered official exceed $50 (with specified exceptions).

instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(B)(3) requires a legislative agent to report specified details for meal/food-and-beverage expenditures only when such payments, aggregated for the same calendar year for a particular covered official, 'exceeded a total of fifty dollars'.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled Ohio provisions define 'legislative agent' qualitatively (e.g., 'main purposes' / 'at least a portion of the individual's time') and require registration within ten days after engagement, but do not set any dollar compensation threshold for when registration is required.
The bundled text requires registration upon engagement and does not provide any expenditure-based dollar threshold triggering registration.
The statute defines 'legislative agent' in terms of 'at least a portion of the individual's time' and 'as one of the individual's main purposes' without specifying any percentage-of-time threshold.

Outside the special $50 threshold for meals/food-and-beverage itemization, the statute does not provide a general de minimis dollar threshold below which lobbyist expenditures need not be reported; statements report totals and itemize when expenditures are made to/for a particular official without a stated minimum.
The bundled Ohio legislative lobbying reporting provisions do not establish any time-based de minimis threshold for filing expenditure/financial-transaction statements.
